A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the paper argues that the power of organisations to influence the policy process is a function of the extent to which the organisation can create dependencies within its task environment, and the extent to which it is successful in controlling sources of uncertainty within the environment.
the public sector is not simply a bureaucratic machine, but rather is an organisation which, like any other organisation, has a power structure.
the paper argues for a power perspective on implementation.

the implementation of policies and programs in the public sector is a complex and dynamic process.
